# Feature matrix

<!-- Generated by scripts/feature-matrix.mjs from docs/features.json. Do not edit; change the JSON and run `node scripts/feature-matrix.mjs`. -->

A cell says `tested` only when an automated test in this repository runs that feature on that target; it says `device` only when a recorded run on a physical device or emulator is named. The evidence, and whether the run used a device, an emulator or a simulator, is listed under [Evidence](#evidence). No `tested` cell claims a physical device.

- **tested**: an automated test runs it on that target.
- **device**: a recorded run on the physical device or emulator verified it; the evidence under `handoff/` is named in the cell.
- **preview**: implemented on main, with no automated test on that target.
- **in progress**: in an open pull request, not on main.
- **no**: not implemented on that target.

## Rendering backends

| Feature                                                | web    | tizen   | webos   | vizio   | ps4     | roku   | android | android-tv | ios     | apple-tv | desktop-linux | desktop-windows | desktop-macos |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------ | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------ | ------- | ---------- | ------- | -------- | ------------- | --------------- | ------------- |
| WebGL backend (`packages/renderer/webgl`)              | tested | preview | preview | preview | tested  | no     | preview | preview    | preview | preview  | tested        | preview         | preview       |
| Desktop runtime in Rust embedding Hermes, without Node | no     | no      | no      | no      | no      | no     | no      | no         | no      | no       | tested        | preview         | preview       |
| Canvas 2D backend (`packages/renderer/canvas`)         | tested | preview | preview | preview | preview | no     | no      | no         | no      | no       | no            | no              | no            |
| Roku SceneGraph backend (`packages/renderer/roku`)     | no     | no      | no      | no      | no      | device | no      | no         | no      | no       | no            | no              | no            |

Notes:

- WebGL backend (`packages/renderer/webgl`), tizen, webos, vizio: Same backend as web. The generated Tizen build is only smoke-run in desktop Chromium; no TV hardware.
- WebGL backend (`packages/renderer/webgl`), android, android-tv, ios, apple-tv: NativeScript canvas host. CI builds the app; no test asserts what it draws.
- WebGL backend (`packages/renderer/webgl`), desktop-windows, desktop-macos: The Rust + Hermes runtime (`packages/host-desktop`). Linux draws the real scene in the host suite, and `packages/platform/tests/cli/desktop-smoke.sh` proves a generated app's first frame. macOS arm64 and Windows x64 build and run the headless runtime tests in the `desktop-runtime` workflow; no window is opened there, so drawing on those systems is unverified.
- Desktop runtime in Rust embedding Hermes, without Node, desktop-windows, desktop-macos: The runtime builds for both and runs its headless tests in CI; no CI job opens a window there, and Windows and macOS app packaging is not implemented.
- Canvas 2D backend (`packages/renderer/canvas`), tizen, webos, vizio: `build <target> --legacy`. The Tizen legacy build is only smoke-run in desktop Chromium.
- Canvas 2D backend (`packages/renderer/canvas`), ps4: `build ps4 --legacy` produces the Canvas 2D variant. No test drives a generated PS4 legacy build; the backend itself is tested on web.
- Roku SceneGraph backend (`packages/renderer/roku`), roku: The shared scene conformance suite ran on the TV. The in-browser fake case remains in the `browser` job.

Notes:

- Host contract (`startApp` / `HostDefinition`), tizen, webos, vizio: Built on `webHost` and `startApp`; the generated build is driven in desktop Chromium, never on a TV.
- Host contract (`startApp` / `HostDefinition`), roku: The host test starts the app through `startApp(rokuHost())` and finds no browser globals on the device.
- Host contract (`startApp` / `HostDefinition`), android, android-tv: `nativeHost` supplies `keys` and `text`; accessibility semantics are absent, not stubbed.
- Host contract (`startApp` / `HostDefinition`), desktop-windows, desktop-macos: The generated entry calls `startApp(desktopHost())` and runs in the Rust + Hermes runtime; `packages/host-desktop/tests/host` drives it on Linux. macOS and Windows build the runtime and run the headless tests, not the host suite.
- Text rendering, roku: Fonts, wrapping, flex text and the device's own metrics were measured on the TV.
- Text selection and copy (`<Text selectable>`), ps4: Pointer-only host: a drag selects with the PS4 browser's mouse; no test drives it on the host.
- Text selection and copy (`<Text selectable>`), roku: No pointer, and the Roku backend draws no selection highlight yet; `selectable` is a no-op.
- Text selection and copy (`<Text selectable>`), desktop-linux: The same WebGL backend and pointer sink as web, but no desktop-runtime test drives a selection.
- Focus and key handling, tizen: `tests/cli/browser-smoke.mjs --tv` (test.yml: projects) presses Enter on the focused row of the generated Tizen build, but in desktop Chromium. No test runs on a Tizen TV or with its remote.
- Focus and key handling, roku: The host test also checks that a held key is one press and that the keyEvents service raises the key.
- Focus visibility policy (`focusVisibility`), tizen, webos, vizio, roku, android-tv, apple-tv: The policy is `always`: the ring is drawn for every focus, as the existing TV focus tests assert.
- Pointer and touch input (`src/sdk/input.ts`), tizen: `tests/cli/browser-smoke.mjs --tv` (test.yml: projects) maps clicks through four viewport sizes on the generated Tizen build, but in desktop Chromium. No test runs on a Tizen TV.
- Pointer and touch input (`src/sdk/input.ts`), android, ios: Touch through `hosts/nativescript/touch.mjs`.
- Touch scrolling (`scroll="touch"` on Row and Column), tizen, webos, vizio, roku, android-tv, apple-tv: Touch scrolling is opt-in for pointer-touch hosts; televisions keep the focus-driven scroll modes, even when the browser reports a mouse (webOS).
- Touch scrolling (`scroll="touch"` on Row and Column), ps4: The PS4 host feeds the same scene pointer and mouse events; no test drives the rail through `ps4Host`.
- Touch scrolling (`scroll="touch"` on Row and Column), android, ios: Same engine through `hosts/nativescript/touch.mjs`; not yet driven on an emulator.
- Touch scrolling (`scroll="touch"` on Row and Column), desktop-linux, desktop-windows, desktop-macos: Mouse and touch drag work through `webHost`; desktop wheel and keyboard scrolling keep their native semantics.
- Desktop pointer behaviour (hover, cursor, context menus, wheel, tooltips), tizen, webos, vizio, roku, android-tv, apple-tv: No hover or secondary click on these hosts (a TV pointer remote clicks, it does not hover); the added handlers are opt-in and change none of their focus behaviour.
- Desktop pointer behaviour (hover, cursor, context menus, wheel, tooltips), desktop-linux: The desktop host feeds the same sink; secondary clicks arrive as button 2 and the wheel in layout pixels. The runtime exposes no cursor-shape API, so `setCursor` is not implemented, and no desktop-runtime test drives a context menu.
- Screen history with keyed focus restore (`createScreenHistory`), tizen, webos, vizio: The browser-TV host delivers its Back key through the same dispatcher and uses the platform exit where it exists; no TV hardware run.
- Screen history with keyed focus restore (`createScreenHistory`), ps4: The console's Back is delivered through the dispatcher; exit reports unavailable.
- Screen history with keyed focus restore (`createScreenHistory`), roku: Back goes through the dispatcher and the host's exitApp; no device run of keyed restore yet.
- Screen history with keyed focus restore (`createScreenHistory`), android, android-tv: Hardware Back goes through the dispatcher; no test asserts keyed restore on a device.
- Screen history with keyed focus restore (`createScreenHistory`), desktop-linux, desktop-windows, desktop-macos: The desktop host does not yet supply a dispatcher or exit action; an app's screen history still traverses its history but root Back has no exit.
- Desktop window chrome (`<TitleBar>`, `desktop.titleBar`), desktop-windows: The hit test maps to `HTCAPTION`/`HT*`, so the OS owns move, resize, snap and the title-bar double-click. Built in CI; no CI job opens a window there, and DWM snap/multi-monitor DPI/RDP are unverified.
- Desktop window chrome (`<TitleBar>`, `desktop.titleBar`), desktop-macos: SDL on Cocoa ignores the `RESIZE_*` hit-test results and a borderless window has no traffic lights: a borderless custom mode runs but is untested, and real macOS chrome waits for an AppKit phase (see handoff/title-bar-design.md).
- Accessibility semantics (`src/sdk/semantics.ts`), desktop-windows, desktop-macos: No accessibility adapter is implemented for these systems: the runtime builds and runs its headless tests, but `__solid.a11y` is absent.
- Shapes, borders, gradients and shadows, web: Tested through the renderer. `startApp(webHost(...))` registers the default shaders.
- Shapes, borders, gradients and shadows, roku: Rounded corners, borders, gradients, four-corner colours and shadows; the forced image-fallback tier also passed 26/26.
- Animation (`animateProp`, transitions), roku: x, y and alpha use SceneGraph `Animation` + `FloatFieldInterpolator`; colour, `scale`, delay, loop and unknown easing fall back to the JavaScript clock. Frame pacing during animation has not been measured.

## App authoring surface

The `/app` entry is the one import an app needs. A cell is `tested` when an automated test builds and drives that surface on the target, and `device` when a recorded run on a device or emulator shows it working.

Notes:

- `/app` components the starter uses (`Screen`, `Text`, `Button`), roku: The starter's button counted three Select presses on the TV.
- `/app` layout and overlay components (`List`, `Spacer`, `Row`, `Column`, `Grid`, overlays), web: Unit tests cover them in jsdom; the generated starter does not use them.
- `/app` hooks (`useHost`, `usePlugin`, `useViewport`, service hooks), web: Unit tests cover the hooks in jsdom; the generated starter does not exercise the service hooks on a target.

Notes:

- `links` (`src/sdk/services.ts`), ios, apple-tv: The in-app open arrives. `simctl openurl` delivery was not delivered in the simulator and stays unverified.
- `notifications` (`src/sdk/services.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: a permission prompt is required.
- `notifications` (`src/sdk/services.ts`), ios: The probe reads the permission state; displaying a notification is not verified in the simulator.
- `push` (`src/sdk/services.ts`), web: Only when the app installs `webAppServices(namespace, registration)` with its own service worker. Not verified end to end.
- `push` (`src/sdk/services.ts`), ios: The app supplies a configured Firebase Messaging instance. Not verified end to end.
- `jobs` (`src/sdk/services.ts`), web: Only with the app's own service worker and Background Sync.
- `jobs` (`src/sdk/services.ts`), ios: The app passes `appleJobs(identifiers)`. Not probed on the simulator.
- `share` (`src/sdk/device.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: it opens the system share sheet.
- `share` (`src/sdk/device.ts`), ios: Availability only: the simulator probe does not present the share sheet.
- `haptics` (`src/sdk/device.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: only a person can feel a vibration.
- `display` (`src/sdk/display.ts`), android, android-tv: Android provider: `getMode().getRefreshRate()`, every mode's rate, and a `DisplayManager.DisplayListener` for changes; the host asks the window for the panel's highest mode at start-up, again after a mode switch, and again when the SurfaceView (re)creates its Surface, and pins the exact mode through `preferredDisplayModeId` at the current resolution. Unit tests: packages/platform/tests/display-service.test.ts and packages/renderer/tests/frame-loop.test.mjs (unit job). Measured on a phone emulator with the guest vsync at 120 Hz: 8.33 ms p50 frame deltas; at 60 Hz: 16.67 ms; an idle scene drew 0 frames. A multi-mode panel switch was not reproduced: the emulator exposes one mode. On a Pixel 7 Pro the start-up-only request left the app at 60 fps while the panel touch-boosted to 120 Hz; the surface and mode requests above are the fix, and the FPS meter now reports the display rate and the frame's own cost so the next device run distinguishes a rate request from a slow frame.
- `keepAwake` (`src/sdk/device.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports denied: headless Chromium refuses the screen wake lock.
- `openExternal` (`src/sdk/device.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: it opens another application.
- `orientation` (`src/sdk/device.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: it rotates the screen.
- `appReview` (`src/sdk/device.ts`), android: Written but not device-verified; the phone probe reports it unavailable.
- `colorScheme` (`src/sdk/theme.tsx`), apple-tv: The service answers. A simulator appearance change was not reported, so live updates stay unverified on tvOS.
- `keyEvents` (`src/sdk/shortcuts.ts`), android: Written but not device-verified; the phone probe reports it unavailable.
- `keyEvents` (`src/sdk/shortcuts.ts`), android-tv: The ArrowDown shortcut did not fire on the TV emulator (the keydown arrived).
- `audio` (`src/sdk/audio.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: it plays sound.
- `mediaSession` (`src/sdk/media.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: it changes the system media controls.
- `fullscreen` (`src/sdk/media.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: it needs a user gesture.
- `fullscreen` (`src/sdk/media.ts`), android-tv: Reports unavailable on the TV emulator.
- `thumbnails` (`src/sdk/media.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: it needs a video to decode.
- `camera` (`src/sdk/capture.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: it asks for the camera.
- `camera` (`src/sdk/capture.ts`), android: Written but not device-verified.
- `microphone` (`src/sdk/capture.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: it asks for the microphone.
- `download` (`src/sdk/download.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: it saves a file.
- `filePicker` (`src/sdk/files.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: it opens the file picker.
- `filePicker` (`src/sdk/files.ts`), android: Written but not device-verified.
- `geolocation` (`src/sdk/geolocation.ts`), web: The showcase probe reports unverified: it asks for the location permission.
- `geolocation` (`src/sdk/geolocation.ts`), android-tv: The TV probe needs a location fix that was not sent to the shared device.
- `biometrics` (`src/sdk/biometrics.ts`), android: Written but not device-verified.
- `biometrics` (`src/sdk/biometrics.ts`), ios: The probe verifies the refusal; a successful authentication needs a person and is not verified.
- `menus` (`src/sdk/menus.ts`), desktop-linux, desktop-windows, desktop-macos: Not provided by the Rust + Hermes host yet.
- `updateDelivery` (`src/sdk/update.ts`), desktop-linux, desktop-windows, desktop-macos: Not provided by the Rust + Hermes host yet.
- `updateSource` (`src/sdk/update.ts`), desktop-linux, desktop-windows, desktop-macos: Not provided by the Rust + Hermes host yet.

Notes:

- Playback adapter (`packages/video`), roku: The adapter owns a SceneGraph Video node beneath the app surface; the player is never stacked above the UI. DRM was not exercised (no licence server); per-player volume is not available (mute only).

## CLI commands

A command is `tested` for a target when a CI job runs it for that target and checks the result.

| `solid-platform build <target>`                           | tested  | tested  | tested  | tested  | tested  | tested  | preview | tested     | tested  | tested   | preview       | preview         | preview       |
| `solid-platform dev <web\|desktop>`                       | preview | no      | no      | no      | no      | no      | no      | no         | no      | no       | preview       | preview         | preview       |
| `solid-platform doctor [target]`                          | tested  | tested  | tested  | tested  | preview | preview | preview | preview    | preview | preview  | preview       | preview         | preview       |
| `solid-platform run <target>`                             | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview    | preview | preview  | preview       | preview         | preview       |
| `solid-platform devices`                                  | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview    | preview | preview  | preview       | preview         | preview       |
| `solid-platform plugin new`                               | tested  | tested  | tested  | tested  | preview | tested  | preview | tested     | tested  | tested   | tested        | preview         | preview       |
| `solid-platform check [target]`                           | tested  | tested  | tested  | tested  | preview | tested  | preview | preview    | preview | preview  | tested        | preview         | preview       |
| `solid-platform explain <target> <module>`                | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview    | preview | preview  | preview       | preview         | preview       |
| `solid-platform package desktop`                          | no      | no      | no      | no      | no      | no      | no      | no         | no      | no       | preview       | preview         | preview       |
| `solid-platform certify roku <metrics.json>`              | no      | no      | no      | no      | no      | preview | no      | no         | no      | no       | no            | no              | no            |
| `solid-platform add video <release.tgz>`                  | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview | preview | tested     | tested  | tested   | preview       | preview         | preview       |
| `solid-platform add desktop [<tarball> \| <url> \| none]` | no      | no      | no      | no      | no      | no      | no      | no         | no      | no       | preview       | preview         | preview       |

Notes:

- `solid-platform build <target>`, desktop-linux: `tests/cli/projects-smoke.sh` builds it only when a runtime is present, and no CI job provides one; `tests/cli/desktop-smoke.sh` builds bytecode and proves a first frame on a machine with a runtime.
- `solid-platform dev <web|desktop>`, web: Implemented for web; no test runs the dev server.
- `solid-platform dev <web|desktop>`, desktop-linux, desktop-windows, desktop-macos: Builds and starts the app in the Rust + Hermes runtime; no automated test covers the dev window.
- `solid-platform run <target>`, web, tizen, webos, vizio, ps4, roku, android, android-tv, ios, apple-tv, desktop-linux, desktop-windows, desktop-macos: Device commands ran against faked tools only; no test installs and launches an app with `run`.
- `solid-platform devices`, web, tizen, webos, vizio, ps4, roku, android, android-tv, ios, apple-tv, desktop-linux, desktop-windows, desktop-macos: Device commands ran against faked tools only; no test lists a real device with this command.
- `solid-platform explain <target> <module>`, web, tizen, webos, vizio, ps4, roku, android, android-tv, ios, apple-tv, desktop-linux, desktop-windows, desktop-macos: The resolver has a unit test (tests/cli/variants.test.mjs); the command is not run for a target in CI.
- `solid-platform package desktop`, desktop-linux, desktop-windows, desktop-macos: The `solid-platform` command is not run in CI; the host's `packageDesktop` is exercised by `packages/host-desktop/tests/package/run.mjs`, and the `Desktop packages` workflow runs only when started by hand.
- `solid-platform add desktop [<tarball> | <url> | none]`, desktop-linux, desktop-windows, desktop-macos: Installs the host package or downloads a prebuilt runtime. Resolution is unit-tested (`tests/cli/unit/add-desktop.test.mjs`); `tests/cli/projects-smoke.sh` installs it only when a built runtime is present, and no CI job provides one.

Notes:

- `Intl` (plural rules, number, date/time, relative time, list and collation), web, tizen, webos, vizio: The browser's own `Intl`; the SDK's formatting is not asserted on these targets.
- `Intl` (plural rules, number, date/time, relative time, list and collation), roku: The device's Hermes has no `Intl`; `sdk/i18n.ts` falls back to `en`.
- `Intl` (plural rules, number, date/time, relative time, list and collation), android, android-tv, ios, apple-tv: The engine's own `Intl`; no target test asserts formatting.
- `Intl` (plural rules, number, date/time, relative time, list and collation), desktop-windows, desktop-macos: The same ICU4X formatters; neither is built with a window in CI.

## Evidence

A `tested` cell names the test file that covers it, the workflow and job that run it, and what it checks. A `device` cell names a recorded run kept under `handoff/`; that folder is local, so the generator checks the shape of the path, not what the run contains.

### Tested

- WebGL backend (`packages/renderer/webgl`), web: packages/platform/tests/webgl/conformance-webgl.test.tsx (test.yml: browser; scene conformance cases on real WebGL in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit)
- WebGL backend (`packages/renderer/webgl`), ps4: packages/platform/tests/webgl/ps4-host.test.tsx (test.yml: browser; a scene mounted through `ps4Host(webHost)` draws in real WebGL in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit)
- WebGL backend (`packages/renderer/webgl`), desktop-linux: packages/host-desktop/tests/scene/run.mjs (desktop-runtime.yml: linux; the shared fixture is rendered in the Rust + Hermes runtime and its pixels compared with Chromium)
- Desktop runtime in Rust embedding Hermes, without Node, desktop-linux: packages/host-desktop/tests/run.sh (desktop-runtime.yml: linux; the runtime opens a window and the host suite runs the scene, input, text fields, services, accessibility, idle and packaging checks)
- Canvas 2D backend (`packages/renderer/canvas`), web: packages/platform/tests/webgl/conformance-canvas.test.tsx (test.yml: browser; scene conformance cases on Canvas 2D in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit)
- Host contract (`startApp` / `HostDefinition`), web: packages/platform/tests/cli/browser-smoke.mjs (test.yml: projects; the generated app starts through `startApp(webHost(...))` in Chromium)
- Host contract (`startApp` / `HostDefinition`), ps4: packages/platform/tests/webgl/ps4-host.test.tsx (test.yml: browser; the scene starts through `startApp(ps4Host(webHost))` in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit)
